metadata.title: Digital Forensics SSPP
metadata.remarks: This SSPP defines the authority, constraints, and requirements for preservation, analysis, and reconstruction of evidentiary truth following security incidents.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP inherits authority, escalation rules, and response constraints and SHALL NOT redefine operational decision-making.

system-characteristics.system-description: Defines requirements for evidentiary preservation, chain of custody, forensic analysis, and post-incident reconstruction to establish defensible truth.

system-implementation.remarks: Digital Forensics is a truth-establishment function. It SHALL NOT be optimized for speed, operational efficiency, or automation beyond evidence integrity requirements.

forensic-scope.description: Collection of digital artifacts, logs, memory, storage, and relevant system state.
Protection of evidence integrity and prevention of contamination or loss.
Analysis and correlation of preserved artifacts to reconstruct timelines and root cause.
Documentation of evidence handling, access, transfer, and retention.

forensic-requirements.statement: All forensic activities SHALL be conducted under the authority of the designated Digital Forensics Authority.
Evidence SHALL be preserved in a manner that prevents unauthorized modification or loss.
All forensic actions SHALL be documented to support traceability and defensibility.
Forensic evidence SHALL be isolated from operational systems where practicable.

forensic-holds.statement: When a forensic hold is declared, all response and automation actions SHALL constrain or suspend activities that risk evidence integrity.
Forensic holds SHALL NOT be overridden by Incident Response or automation under any circumstances.

control-implementation.description: Controls ensure evidentiary integrity, accountability, and defensibility of forensic outcomes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Incident evidence is collected, protected, and retained.
Post-incident analysis supports corrective action and accountability.
Audit and forensic data are protected from unauthorized modification or deletion.
Forensic records are retained to support investigation and legal requirements.

statements.statement: Digital Forensics SHALL operate independently of Security Operations performance objectives.
Automation SHALL NOT perform forensic analysis or alter forensic evidence.
Incident Response SHALL NOT sacrifice evidence integrity for containment speed.
Forensic conclusions SHALL NOT be modified to support operational narratives.

back-matter.remarks: All SecOps SSPPs involving response, automation, and escalation SHALL defer to this SSPP once a forensic hold is declared.
